clue.text: Lead put into gold (two billion) in only a bit of a lather!

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces before it go inside the word for only

parts.note: only, as in sole survivor, means sole

indicators.note: put into says the chemical symbol for lead is placed inside the symbol for gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
B is a standard abbreviation for billion, so two of them give BB

explanation.surface: An alchemist's metals and vast sums of money end up as nothing more than lather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a verb or a leash but is the metal. 'put into' nests one symbol in the other, and 'in' sends that plus the two billions inside the word for only.
explanation.definitionFit: A single sphere of soapy film is a tiny piece of the froth called lather.

clue.text: Punch magazine finally set up trial for gripping collection

parts.note: to sock someone is to punch them

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word magazine
set up in a down clue means the word for trial is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a trial is a test

explanation.surface: Punch, the old humour magazine, puts a gripping anthology on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns TEST into TSET in this down entry. Punch was a long-running British satirical magazine, which is the false path.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of sockets for a ratchet wrench is a collection of tools that grip nuts.

clue.text: Drug resistance is involved in biting

indicators.note: is involved in says the abbreviation for resistance goes inside the word for the drug

parts.note: acid is slang for the drug LSD
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Resistance is involved in biting drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrid smell or remark is sharp and pungent, as biting as acid.

clue.text: Veritable old oddball holding ring is no in-law

indicators.note: holding says the rearranged letters wrap round the circle shape
oddball suggests something strange or eccentric, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A truly eccentric old character with a ring is not related by marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddball' rearranges the twelve letters, and 'holding' wraps them round the ring shape. 'is' is just a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative by blood is kin by birth, as opposed to one acquired through marriage.

clue.text: Recess with table extension may add to enjoyment of meal

definitions.text: may add to enjoyment of meal

parts.note: a bay is a recess in a wall or room, as in a bay window
a leaf is a hinged or removable board that extends a table

explanation.surface: An alcove and an extending table make dinner more pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic herb is added to stews and soups to improve their flavour.

clue.text: Seabird endlessly trailing hurls seafood

indicators.note: trailing says the shortened bird comes after the word for hurls

parts.note: to lob something is to hurl it high

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the bird is dropped

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird follows, trailing behind as someone throws fish scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the bird's final letter, and 'trailing' puts what is left behind the throws.
explanation.definitionFit: The lobster is a large shellfish eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Pressure since student's first exam success

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
since, as in 'since you ask', means as

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word student's

explanation.surface: A student under pressure gets through a first examination.
explanation.definitionFit: To get through an exam is to obtain a passing grade, a basic examination success.

clue.text: Rambling late, one confident in one's own time

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
to be sure is to be confident

explanation.surface: Wandering in late, someone sure of themselves takes their own sweet time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at leisure means doing it without hurry, at a pace one chooses.

clue.text: Kid possibly influenced in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: someone swayed by an argument is influenced by it

explanation.surface: A child may be persuaded by a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but kid is also goat leather, an example of a soft napped leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid leather from young goats can be finished as a soft napped leather, so kid is an example.

clue.text: Coat regularly cut in bear with red hair?

indicators.note: cut in says the selected letters are inserted into the word for bear

parts.note: to bear a load is to carry it

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the word coat, here its second and fourth

explanation.surface: A ginger bear has its coat trimmed at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of Coat, and 'cut in' sets them inside the word for bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair the colour of the orange root vegetable is a jocular description of red hair.

clue.text: Uneven writing from shifty Liberal

indicators.note: shifty suggests letters that will not stay put, so the word Liberal is rearranged

explanation.surface: A slippery Liberal politician produces some lopsided prose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifty' rearranges the letters of LIBERAL. 'Uneven' sounds like a criticism of the writing but means raised and bumpy to the touch.
explanation.definitionFit: The tactile script for the blind uses raised dots, so the page surface is literally uneven.

clue.text: An entry, After Midnight, followed by Madness song?

parts.note: an entry is a way in
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, the hours after midnight
madness can mean rage, as in mad with anger

explanation.surface: A pop single by the ska band Madness is entered for a late-night show.
explanation.walkthrough: Madness was a British ska band, After Midnight sounds like a title; both are mere pieces. 'followed by' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known Christmas carol, so an example of a song, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Sold when volume's left over

indicators.note: left, as in departed, says the abbreviation for volume goes from the word for sold

parts.note: to sell goods from a stall or machine is to vend them, so sold means vended
V is the standard abbreviation for volume; the 's here stands for is

explanation.surface: Goods are sold once the remaining volume has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' sits at the end looking like part of 'left over' but it is the definition, as in 'the game is over'.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is finished or concluded, we say it is over.

clue.text: Surplus weight loss scheme achieving ultimate turnaround? Send away for trial!

parts.note: surplus stock is extra stock

indicators.note: ultimate turnaround swaps only the final pair of letters of the diet word

parts.note: a diet is a plan for losing weight

explanation.surface: A slimmer's plan that reverses at the end might get someone shipped off to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate turnaround' reverses just the last two letters of DIET, giving DITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Extradition is the handing over of a suspect to another country to stand trial there.

clue.text: St-sticks suggested for outdoor fixtures?

parts.note: St is short for a road in a town, and sticks is slang for pieces of furniture, so the clue reads as road furniture

explanation.surface: Road-side poles are proposed as permanent outdoor fittings.
explanation.definitionFit: Benches, lamp posts and bollards fixed along public roads are collectively called this.

clue.text: Diamonds and Greek letter on top of military vehicles

indicators.note: on top of in a down clue puts the Greek letter above the rest

parts.note: rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet
M is an abbreviation for military
buses are passenger vehicles

explanation.surface: Army transports bear a diamond emblem and a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a four-sided figure with equal sides, the diamond shape.

clue.text: Some detail of xenophobia, being brought up in Slough

indicators.note: being brought up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards
some says only part of the run of letters is wanted

explanation.surface: A slice of xenophobia is being raised in the town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here it is a verb: to shed skin. Reading 'detail of xe' backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To slough off dead skin is to shed it, which is what exfoliating does.

clue.text: Denied game point and played on

definitions.meaning: read literally, removed the advantage, the tennis score that is one point from winning a game, from an opponent
played on, as in played on someone's fears, means exploited

explanation.definitionFit: To exploit someone's weakness is to play on it, and also to use it to one's benefit.

clue.text: Very twisty col on a kind of mountain

indicators.note: twisty suggests something bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A very winding mountain pass leads up a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisty' rearranges COL ON A to OLCANO.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano is a mountain formed by eruptions of lava and ash.

clue.text: None picked up stick in race with person chasing

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue says the word is lifted, read from bottom to top

parts.note: in a relay race the runners pass a baton
in the playground game of tag the player who chases is called it

explanation.surface: A relay runner picks up the dropped baton as someone chases them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns BATON to NOTAB in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'not at all' or 'none whatsoever' is an idiomatic way to say none.

clue.text: California spirit with hired convertible

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
brio is spirit or verve
a flat that is let has been hired out

explanation.surface: In California, spirited folk hire a soft-top car.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a car with a folding roof, the same thing as a convertible.

clue.text: Contract problem in small print?

definitions.meaning: a hidden snag buried in the fine print of an agreement

explanation.definitionFit: Catching a cold means contracting it, and a hidden snag in a deal is a drawback.

clue.text: A northern Scandinavian recoiling in shock

indicators.note: recoiling suggests springing backwards, so the word for the northern people is read in reverse

parts.note: a Lapp is a person from Lapland, in the far north of Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A man from the Arctic north recoils in horror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recoiling' turns only the Arctic people backwards; the opening A stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to fill them with horror, to shock them deeply.

clue.text: I'm rather left to hold to mat in wrestling and floor in boxing

parts.note: to pin an opponent is to hold them down on the wrestling mat
KO is short for knockout, flooring an opponent

explanation.surface: A left-leaning wrestler and boxer describes their combat sports.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks as the answer. Pinning and knocking out make the sporting picture.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a derogatory term for someone with mild socialist leanings, somewhat left-wing.

clue.text: Piece of picture from period between Woodlanders and Jude?

parts.note: Thomas Hardy wrote The Woodlanders, then Tess of the d'Urbervilles, then Jude the Obscure, so Tess comes between them
an era is a period of history

explanation.surface: A literary critic asks for a part of an image from Hardy's middle period.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy's novels in order: The Woodlanders (1887), Tess of the d'Urbervilles (1891), Jude the Obscure (1895).
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one small tile in a mosaic, so a single piece of a picture.

clue.text: Plant engineers gain OBE

indicators.note: engineers, as a verb, means arranges or contrives, so these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Engineers receive an honour from the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineers' looks like the subject of the sentence but is a verb that rearranges GAIN and OBE. An OBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The begonia is a flowering plant popular in gardens and pots.

clue.text: Heads from Hull University should know Hull

indicators.note: heads from asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Staff at Hull University should know who's in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Hull' suggests the city, but the final word is the definition: the outer casing of a seed.
explanation.definitionFit: The hull of a seed or grain is its dry outer covering, also called the husk.

clue.text: Encourage old prime minister in placement for wards?

parts.note: to foster a talent is to encourage it
Sir Alec Douglas-Home was British prime minister in 1963 and 1964

explanation.surface: A former premier encourages a new housing scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Children in care, wards of the state, are placed with families in such a household.
